dva-ini-013.text: A developer is creating his first function AWS Lambda in Python. What is the role of the handler in the function?
options: It is the method of entry that the Lambda invokes when performing the function, receiving the event and the context as parameters
It is the log generated automatically after each execution
It is the network configuration file of the function
It is the web server that the developer needs to install in the function
dva-ini-013.explanation: The handler is the input point configured in the function (e.g. lambda_function.lambda_handler): at each invocation, the service calls it passing the event object and the execution context.
dva-ini-013.hint: It is the code's 'entry door': the method the service calls with (event, context)).
optionRationales: The handler is the input point configured in the function (e.g. lambda_function.lambda_handler): at each invocation, the service calls it passing the event object and the execution context.
Lambda is serverless — no web server to install; runtime invokes handler directly.
Network Settings (VPC) are defined in function configuration, not in handler, which is code.
Logs go to the CloudWatch Logs — the handler is the executed code, not the execution record.

dva-ini-014.text: A function Lambda it needs to connect to different endpoints according to the environment (dev points to the API of tests, prod for real), without changing the code between environments. Lambda attends to this in a simple way for non-sensitive values?
options: Save fixed endpoints to code and comment unused lines
Store endpoints in a volume EBS attached to function
Function environment variables, read by code in execution time
Create a completely different function for each endpoint
dva-ini-014.explanation: Environment variables allow parameterization of the function by environment (URLs, flags, resource names) without code change — the default mechanism for non-sensitive configuration.
dva-ini-014.hint: Settings that change by environment, read in runtime: the classic key-value pair of function configuration.
optionRationales: Environment variables allow parameterization of the function by environment (URLs, flags, resource names) without code change — the default mechanism for non-sensitive configuration.
Alternating comments on the code is manual, error-prone and requires new deployment at each exchange — exactly what you want to avoid.
Duplicate functions multiplies maintenance — the same function should serve environments via configuration.
Functions Lambda do not attach volumes EBS — storage and configuration follow other mechanisms.

dva-ini-015.text: Various functions Lambda of the same project use the same heavy libraries (ex: SDK of a partner and internal utilities). Today each deployment package repeats these dependencies. Lambda allows you to share these libraries between functions, reducing the size of packages?
options: Install libraries manually on the server of Lambda
Lambda Layers: layers with shared dependencies, attached to functions
Hosting libraries in a pocket S3 public
Increase the memory of functions to behave packages
dva-ini-015.explanation: Layers pack libraries and common content separately from the code: several functions refer to the same layer, reducing duplication and the size of each deployment.
dva-ini-015.hint: Think of the reusable 'layers' that are below the code of each function.
optionRationales: Layers pack libraries and common content separately from the code: several functions refer to the same layer, reducing duplication and the size of each deployment.
Memory does not resolve duplication of dependencies in deployment packages.
Download Public Bucket Dependencies in Runtime is insecure and slow — the native mechanism is the layers.
No server accessible for manual installation on Lambda — the environment is managed by AWS.

dva-ini-016.text: A developer plans to use AWS Lambda for processing that may take up to 30 Why this choice is inadequate and what is the relevant limit?
options: The maximum execution time of a function Lambda is of 15 minutes; longer processes should use alternatives like ECS/Fargate or Step Functions dividing the work
The Lambda has no time limit, the problem is just the cost
The Lambda only performs functions of up to 30 seconds
The Lambda requires the purchase of reserved capacity to pass from 5 minutes
dva-ini-016.explanation: The configurable maximum timeout of Lambda It's 900 seconds (15 minutes) — larger tasks need to be broken in steps or moved to long run services.
dva-ini-016.hint: The watch of the Lambda Cut the execution in a quarter of an hour — bigger jobs need another home.
optionRationales: The configurable maximum timeout of Lambda It's 900 seconds (15 minutes) — larger tasks need to be broken in steps or moved to long run services.
The limit is not 30 seconds — this value is the standard timeout for integration of API Gateway, not the maximum of Lambda.
There is a strict limit of 15 minutes — execution is terminated when it is reached, regardless of cost.
There is no purchase of capacity to extend the timeout — the limit of 15 minutes is good for everyone.

dva-ini-017.text: One API created in Amazon API Gateway needs separate URLs for the development and production environments (e.g. /dev and /prod), each of which can point to different versions and configurations of the same API. What concept of API Gateway implements this separation?
options: Resources, which divide API by environment
Models, which validate environments
Use plans, which create environments for user groups
Internships (stages), which publish API in distinct environments with their own configurations
dva-ini-017.explanation: Each stage is a 'publication' named by the API (dev, staging, prod) URL, independent variables and configurations — allowing to evolve and test without affecting production.
dva-ini-017.hint: Each 'Palco' from API has your own URL and audience: dev, approval, production.
optionRationales: Each stage is a 'publication' named by the API (dev, staging, prod) URL, independent variables and configurations — allowing to evolve and test without affecting production.
Resources define the paths (routes) of API, as /orders — do not separate publication environments.
Use plans control limits and consumption quotas per key of API — do not publish distinct environments.
Models define payload validation schemes — unrelated to environment separation.

dva-ini-018.text: A developer models a table of the DynamoDB to store chat messages: you need to search for all messages of a conversation sorted by date/hour. Which primary key design meets this access?
options: Only partition key = message text
Composite key: partition key = conversation ID and sort key = message timestamp
No primary key, leaving the DynamoDB sort alone
Only partition key = message timestamp
dva-ini-018.explanation: The composite key groups the items from the same conversation in the partition and keeps them sorted by the key spell — a Query by the conversation ID returns messages in chronological order.
dva-ini-018.hint: Group by 'dono' (partition) and sort by 'when' (order key).
optionRationales: The composite key groups the items from the same conversation in the partition and keeps them sorted by the key spell — a Query by the conversation ID returns messages in chronological order.
With the timestamp as the partition key, messages from the same conversation spread and there's no way to get them together efficiently.
The content of the message does not identify the conversation or provide ordination — unfeasible as a key to access.
All table of DynamoDB requires defined primary key — and ordination exists only within the partition via spell key.

dva-ini-019.text: A table of the DynamoDB uses the order ID as the primary key, but the application also needs to search for orders by the customer ID efficiently. Which feature allows these queries without scanning the entire table?
options: Increase the reading capacity of the table
Run Scan with Customer Filter in each search
Create a second table by manually copying the data
A global secondary index (GSI) with customer ID as partition key
dva-ini-019.explanation: The GSI creates a view of the table indexed by another attribute: customer queries use Query in the index instead of Scan in the table — efficient and economical.
dva-ini-019.hint: To ask for another attribute without sweeping everything, create a second indexed gate — global.
optionRationales: The GSI creates a view of the table indexed by another attribute: customer queries use Query in the index instead of Scan in the table — efficient and economical.
Scan reads the whole table and filters after — slow and expensive, exactly what indices avoid.
Manual copy generates inconsistency and duplicated work — the GSI does the projection automatically.
More capacity accelerates inefficient Scan without changing its full scan nature.

dva-ini-020.text: In a Node.js application, the developer needs to send objects to S3, read items from DynamoDB and post messages in SNS, all from the code. AWS provides for programmatic interaction with services from the application?
options: The Management Console of AWS built-in application
The AWS SDK for the application language (ex: AWS SDK for JavaScript)
A Connection SSH direct with each service
The AWS CloudFormation
dva-ini-020.explanation: The SDK encapsulates calls to the APIs of AWS in the language of the developer — authentication, signature of requests, withdrawals and types ready for use in the code.
dva-ini-020.hint: The official 'toolbox' in each language to speak with the APIs of AWS inside the code.
optionRationales: The SDK encapsulates calls to the APIs of AWS in the language of the developer — authentication, signature of requests, withdrawals and types ready for use in the code.
The console is the web interface for humans — applications use SDKs/APIs, not console pages.
Managed services do not expose SSH — the interaction is via APIs HTTPS Encapsulated by hair SDK.
CloudFormation provide infrastructure declaratively — is not the service call library within the application code.

dva-ini-021.text: A developer configured the AWS CLI on your machine with the command 'aws configure'. What information this command stores to authenticate calls?
options: The account credit card number
Only the account name AWS
Access Key ID, Secret Access Key, Default Region and Output Format
Management console user and password
dva-ini-021.explanation: The 'aws configure' saves credentials (key and secret access) and preferences (region and format) in profile files (~/.aws/credentials and ~/.aws/config), used to sign calls from CLI.
dva-ini-021.hint: These are the two programmatic 'keys' + two preferences (where and how to respond).
optionRationales: The 'aws configure' saves credentials (key and secret access) and preferences (region and format) in profile files (~/.aws/credentials and ~/.aws/config), used to sign calls from CLI.
A CLI does not use console login — uses programmatic credentials (access keys or temporary credentials)).
Payment data belongs to the billing record — never used to authenticate calls from API.
Account name doesn't authenticate anything — calls require cryptographic credentials.

dva-ini-022.text: In an order architecture, the checkout service must continue to work even when the billing service is out of the air, delivering the tasks to it as soon as it returns. AWS Uncouple these components with a durable message queue?
options: Amazon SQS
Amazon Route 53
AWS X-Ray
Amazon CloudFront
dva-ini-022.explanation: The SQS store messages in a durable way until they are consumed: checkout publishes and follows, and billing processes at its pace — classic disconnect between producer and consumer.
dva-ini-022.hint: The durable dimmer between who produces and who consumes tasks.
optionRationales: The SQS store messages in a durable way until they are consumed: checkout publishes and follows, and billing processes at its pace — classic disconnect between producer and consumer.
The Route 53 resolve DNS — does not store or deliver messages between services.
The CloudFront delivery of cache content to end-users — no messaging mechanism between microservices.
X-Ray tracks requirements for performance analysis — does not carry business messages.

dva-ini-023.text: A developer needs to decide between Amazon SNS and Amazon SQS for two streams: (A) immediately notify several interested systems when an event occurs; (B) accumulate tasks for a single worker to process at their own pace. What is the correct association?
options: SQS for flow A and SNS for flow B
SNS for flow A (push publication for multiple subscribers) and SQS for flow B (line pull for a consumer))
SQS for both flows
SNS for both flows
dva-ini-023.explanation: SNS is immediate delivery pub/sub to several subscribers; SQS is a durable row consumed by polling — the classic double message, often combined (fan-out)).
dva-ini-023.hint: Topic shouts for all the subscribers (push); line guard for who comes to fetch (pull).
optionRationales: SNS is immediate delivery pub/sub to several subscribers; SQS is a durable row consumed by polling — the classic double message, often combined (fan-out)).
Invested: row does not distribute copies to several stakeholders, and topic does not accumulate tasks for subsequent consumption at its own pace.
The SNS does not hold messages for a worker to look for later — without subscriber available on delivery, flow B would fail.
One row delivers each message to a single consumer — does not simultaneously distribute to several A-flow systems.

dva-ini-024.text: An e-commerce application wants to react to events like 'created order' by route them to different destinations according to the content (orders above R$ 1.000 go for anti-fraud analysis; the others, for the standard flow), using declarative rules without routing code. What service provides this bus of events with rules?
options: Amazon S3 Event Notifications
Amazon EventBridge
AWS CloudTrail
Amazon ElestiCache
dva-ini-024.explanation: The EventBridge is the event bus with content filtering rules: event patterns decide the destination (Lambda, SQS, Step Functions) no routing logic in the application.
dva-ini-024.hint: The 'event point' where rules read content and choose destination.
optionRationales: The EventBridge is the event bus with content filtering rules: event patterns decide the destination (Lambda, SQS, Step Functions) no routing logic in the application.
Notifications from the S3 trigger only events of the bucket itself (creation/removal of objects) — do not route arbitrary business events by content rules.
The CloudTrail records calls from API for audit — no application event bus.
ElastiCache is cached in memory — without any event routing function.
